passage:
Interviewer: Was it hard to say no to your partner?

I'm Baljeet. Very. Kiran and I had been together a year, and one night I just wasn't in the mood, though it wasn't about Kiran. I lay there thinking, if I say no, Kiran will be disappointed, maybe think I've stopped caring. My stomach was in knots. Finally I said, "I love being close to you, but tonight I'm not ready. It isn't anything you did." Kiran was quiet for a second, then said, "Thank you for telling me. We can just talk." That was it. No sulking. I remember thinking that if Kiran had kept pushing, that would have been a signal to speak to someone I trust. But Kiran didn't. My comfort mattered as much as Kiran's wishes, and I finally believed it.

qa.q: How long had Baljeet and Kiran been together?
What was Baljeet afraid of before saying no?
qa.a: That Kiran would be disappointed and might think Baljeet had stopped caring, which left Baljeet's stomach in knots.

qa.q: What did Baljeet say that helped, and what would have been a warning sign?
qa.a: Baljeet said kindly and clearly that Baljeet wasn't ready and that it wasn't Kiran's doing. Repeated pressure after a no would have been the warning sign to talk to someone trusted.

qa.q: How did Kiran respond, and what does it show?
qa.a: Kiran thanked Baljeet, offered to just talk and did not sulk, which shows Kiran respected Baljeet's comfort as much as Kiran's own wishes.

grounding: Shows not being ready and fearing to disappoint a partner, saying no kindly and clearly, and the partner respecting it, with repeated pressure named as a warning sign.

passage:
The employee wellness counselling room had a box of tissues and a plant nobody watered. Saurabh sat forward, elbows on knees.

"It's embarrassing," he said. "My wife, Nazia, wants us to be close more often. Physically. And I'm just... not ready most nights. Work, my father's illness. I keep saying yes because I'm scared she'll feel rejected. Then I feel worse."

Francis, the counsellor, listened without interrupting. "Your comfort matters just as much as hers. Saying no kindly is allowed. Saying yes when you mean no doesn't really protect her."

"What if she's hurt?"

"She might be, for a moment. You can say it warmly: I love you, I'm not up to it tonight, can we just be together? A caring partner can hear that." Francis paused. "And if it ever turns into repeated pressure, I'd want you to come back and talk to someone about that."

Saurabh breathed out. "Okay. I'll try tonight."

qa.q: What two things did Saurabh say were weighing on him?
What was Saurabh feeling about saying yes when he didn't want to?
qa.a: Saurabh felt scared of hurting Nazia and then worse afterwards, embarrassed and conflicted.

qa.q: What did Francis advise, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Francis said Saurabh's comfort matters equally and he can say no kindly, because saying yes while meaning no doesn't truly protect either of them.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel if Saurabh says no warmly?
qa.a: Nazia might feel briefly disappointed, but if she cares, she will likely understand and value his honesty.

grounding: The counselling scene shows a young husband afraid of disappointing his wife learning his comfort matters, that he can say no kindly and that repeated pressure is a warning sign.

passage:
Dear Parul,

You're the only one I can write this to. Since the wedding, I've felt I have to say yes whenever Mohan wants to be close. Even when I'm exhausted. Even when I'm just not ready. I'm scared he'll be disappointed, or that his family will hear something.

Last Friday I tried what you told me. I said, gently, "I love you, but I'm not ready tonight." My heart was pounding.

He was quiet, then said, "Okay." And he held my hand. I nearly cried with relief.

But on Sunday he sulked all day and said, "Other wives don't make their husbands beg." That scared me.

I know now my comfort matters as much as his. If Sunday happens again, I'm going to talk to my mother, or the counsellor at the women's centre you told me about. I'm writing it here so I don't talk myself out of it.

Ganga

qa.q: What did Mohan say on Sunday?
qa.a: He said, "Other wives don't make their husbands beg."

qa.q: How did Ganga feel when Mohan held her hand on Friday?
qa.a: Ganga felt so relieved she nearly cried, after being scared of disappointing him.

qa.q: What plan has Ganga made in case the pressure repeats?
qa.a: Ganga plans to talk to her mother or the counsellor at the women's centre, and writes it down so as not to back out.

qa.q: How might Parul feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Parul would likely feel worried about Sunday's remark but glad Ganga tried saying no and has a plan.

grounding: The letter shows a young wife learning she can say no kindly, noticing repeated pressure as a warning sign and planning to talk to someone trusted.
